Prompt_Content: Review the entire repository and remove any instances of the terms 'actuarially proven', 'actuarially sound', or similar variations. Replace them with language stating that the models are 'actuarially informed concepts awaiting formal review'. Add a global disclaimer in the footer or terms page emphasizing that the captive models only insure 'fortuitous risk' (accidental/unforeseen events) and not 'speculative risk'.

Create a new page detailing 'Home Gap Coverage.' Explain this concept by drawing a direct analogy to automotive gap coverage. Detail how it protects buyers and builders from the delta between the expected cost of an ADU/prefab installation and the actual cost caused by fortuitous events (e.g., unforeseen site foundation issues, sudden material shortages). Draft a sample policy slip for this coverage.

Update the '12 General Contractors' section. Frame the captive as a tool to incentivize GCs to specialize in prefab installations. Use the analogy of a corporate business unit insuring its product R&D. Explain how GCs can pay premiums to smooth out cash flow and protect against the fortuitous risks of adopting new prefab installation techniques.

Create a new section focusing on the Rural and Student Housing markets. Introduce a 'Mortgage-as-a-Service' (MaaS) concept. Describe how a conceptual API (like Pyron) could be integrated into the site, allowing developers or individuals to apply for ADU mortgages directly on the platform to secure funding for their builds.

Design a conceptual UI/UX section (or mock component) for a 'Tenant Portal'. Explain that for large property owners who build villages of prefabs, the Integral Mass captive allows them to offer in-house renter's insurance. Outline a tech stack that includes an API, a web form, and a chatbot to process renter claims and independent fortuitous risks.

Update the structural model of Integral Mass. Introduce the concept of a 'Cell Captive' or Protected Cell Company (PCC). Explain how, as the system grows, suites of general contractors or property owners can create their own 'cells' beneath the Integral Mass umbrella to capture and pool their specific housing market risks.
